When an external dynamic pressure is applied on a fiber, with the elapse of time, the resulting lateral pressure exerted on the fiber causes its structure to experience expansion and contraction under parametric changes of coating layers. It is shown when the pressure has a tensile form, at some given time, the microbending loss of the fiber attain negative value, which practically results in no loss in the transmissions

articleTitle: Method of Realization of High-Precision Measurement of Lengths of Optical Fibre
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: In the report the method of realization of high-precision measurement of length of the optical fiber based on a principle of working of the circuit of optical "extinction" of polarized laser radiation is discussed. On the basis of the given method it is planned upgrades of the State standard of energy units of capacity and time of distribution of laser pulse and continuous radiation of very-low levels in material mediums

articleTitle: Transformation of Laser Pulse Energy on Wavelength 1.06 Micron with Platinum Bolometer
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: A transformation coefficient of platinum bolometer of laser pulse energy on wavelength 1.06 micron for E-polarized radiation has been determined. A nonlinearity of transformation characteristic of the bolometer and nonuniformity of incident energy distribution along the bolometer length have been kept in mind. An analysis of errors of obtained transformation coefficient of the bolometer has been carried out

articleTitle: Offset Frequency Locking for Pulsed CO2 Waveguide Laser with Two Channels
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: This paper studies the active offset frequency locking for the Q-switched/cavity-dumped z-fold RF excited waveguide CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser with two channels. The method of frequency locking is simple and applicable not only for short pulse CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser but also for many other kinds of short pulse lasers

articleTitle: Simulation of Parameter Fabry-Perot Resonator by Envelope Functions of Multi-Beam Spectra Interferention
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The method for obtaining the analytical expressions of envelope functions in multi-beam spectra of interferention by the single-layer resonator Fabry-Perot is proposed. The method is proposed for normal and oblique incidence of light for transparent and absorbing media

articleTitle: Control of Modes Coupling, Selection and Enhancement in Wavelength-Scale Optical Microcavity Structures: Applications to Microlasers and Biosensing
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Recent advances and remaining challenges in spectral engineering of wavelength-scale optical microcavity structures supporting modes with narrow linewidths, wide mode spacing, directional emission, and greatly enhanced sensitivity to the environmental changes will be reviewed. General recipes for efficient control and manipulation of modes coupling and selective enhancement in such structures will be discussed

articleTitle: Transmission Limitations in DWDM Systems by Stimulated Raman Scattering for Different Types of Fibres
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The mathematical model is considered, that enables to estimate influence of such nonlinear phenomenon as stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) on an overall performance of a communication system. Dependence of the maximal length of the communication line limited by SRS effect on an interval between channels, their quantities in system, bit rate and different types of optical fibres is calculated

articleTitle: Measuring of Optical Radiation Parameters by Receiver with Two Wire Grids
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The receivers of the optical radiation with two grids by purpose to measure the electromagnetic radiation intensity distribution are investigated

articleTitle: Integral Equation Computation of Coupled Propagation Modes in Non-Symmetric Grating Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: A rigorous integral equation formulation in conjunction with Green's function theory is used for the analysis of the wave guiding and coupling phenomena in non-symmetric grating assisted optical couplers. The integral equation is solved by applying an entire domain Galerkin's technique. Numerical results, referring to the evolution of the propagation constants, as function of the grating's characteristics are presented

articleTitle: Trap Detector - for Measurement of Pulse Energy Laser Radiation
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Usually the trap detector is used for measurement of absolute value of power of continuous radiation. In the report it is informed on use the trap detector on the basis of silicon photodiodes for measurement of energy of pulse laser radiation in an optical range. Theoretical principles of such a method of measurement of energy are formulated. The experimental sample of measuring instrument is created. In the report date of experimental investigation this measuring instrument are resulted. Measurements were carried out at various width (100 mus - 500 mus) and forms of pulses. Energy of pulses varied in limits (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> - 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> J). It is established, that accuracy of measurement of energy of pulse laser radiation by such method makes less than one percent and practically does not depend on the form of a pulse. On the basis of such measuring instrument probably creation simple and precision portable a measuring instrument of energy of pulses of laser radiation

articleTitle: Resonant Two-Photon Annihilation of an Electron-Positron Pair in the Light Wave Field
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Resonant two-photon annihilation of an electron-positron pair in the field of a moderately strong circularly polarized wave is investigated theoretically

articleTitle: Research of the Gas HCN- Laser of Terahertz Frequency Band with Anomalous Secondary Emission Hollow Cathode
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Hollow cathode with anomalous secondary emission was applied in the gas terahertz HCN - laser. The laser had stable generation during 8 hours with a charge interval of 0.8 m, the voltage and the current are accordingly 660 V and 0.5 A; the temperature of a radiator of the cathode was +20deg C

articleTitle: Off-Axial Laser Effect in 1D Photonic Crystal with Active Layers
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: We present the results of calculations of the spectral characteristics of finite length 1D PC with air-glass-doped layers. For these calculations we used the transfer matrix formalism. We present also the results of calculation accounting nonlinear deformation of the field distribution along the structure due to gain and refraction index saturation. The results of calculations of laser power are presented on the dependence from gain

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of Heterodyne-Type Laser Doppler Velocimeter Operating Via Long Optical Fiber Guide
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: We present a mathematical model of the signal and noise components in the heterodyne-type laser Doppler velocimeter (LDV) which operates via long optical fiber guide. Our model accounts for laser power output, the length of the optical fiber guide, its absorption, the Rayleigh and Brillouin scattering in the optical fiber guide, and the photo detector parameters. The scattering properties of the moving particles in the liquid or gas flow which is accessed by the LDV are accounted for by an integral scattering coefficient. We show that the Rayleigh and Brillouin scattering in the optical fiber are the principal noise sources that corrupt the signal-to-noise ratio of the present LDV. The numerical examples show that Ae SNR can be as low as 0 dB in the case of the typical optical fibers of a length of several kilometers

articleTitle: Stabilization of femtosecond optical frequency comb at 633 Iodine-stabilized Helium-Neon laser
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: In the report, the outcomes of a building of a system of stabilization and measurement of the main frequency parameters of optical frequency combs of femtosecond laser are submitted. For measurement f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ceo</sub> it is offered to use He-Ne/<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">127</sup>I <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser (lambda = 0.63 mum) with stabilization on hyperfine components "f". Usage He-Ne/<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">127</sup>I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser for stabilization frequency combs will allow to create a means of measurement of absolute frequencies of radiation of semiconducting lasers in optical and near IR ranges

articleTitle: Experimental Realization of Light Beams with Vortical Component for Micro-Manipulation Problems
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Experimental realization of spiral beams and related light beams with phase singularities is considered. The beams have various intensity shape and may be constructed with the help of purely phase transparents. The results of experiments of the beam usage for microobject manipulation are also described

articleTitle: Numerical Modelling a Populations Differences Dynamics of the Resonant Levels of Atoms in a Nonrectangular Form Laser Pulse: Optical Bistability Effect
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The results of numeric calculation of population kinetics of resonant levels for atoms in the non-rectangular form laser pulse on the basis of the modified Bloch equations are presented. Cited equations describe an interaction between two-level atoms ensemble and resonant radiation with an account of the atomic dipole-dipole interaction. It has been found for a case of ch<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> laser pulse a strengthen possibility of manifestation of the internal optical bistability effect special features in the temporary dynamics of populations for the atomic resonant levels under adiabatic slow changing the acting field intensity in comparison with a case of the rectangular form pulses

articleTitle: Penetration of Silver Granules into Quartz Glass Under Powerful Laser Beam Action
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: We investigated the granular silver films deposited on the surface of quartz glass plate, and found that silver granules penetrate into pores of the quartz, when irradiated by a powerful laser beam (we used a CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-laser, lambda= 10.6 mum power P = 8 W). The penetration is caused, firstly, by melting of silver because of heating, and secondly, by a photoeffect on silver granules and capture of electrons by traps of the quartz, plate. The electrostatic field leads to migration of Ag ions into the surface layer of quartz. We investigated the dependence of properties of the waveguide on beam exposition. The measurements of reflection coefficient and refractive index reveal that a step-type waveguide (for red and infra-red light) is created under the surface of quartz. Also we investigated the absorption band of a colloidal solution of Ag in quartz. The band's position reveals that silver occupies less than one tenth of waveguide volume. Typical granule radius inside quartz is 3 nm. It is revealed with microphotographs

articleTitle: Ultrashort Pulse Generation by Gain Switching using Spice Simulator
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Gain switching characteristics of quantum well (QW) lasers diode is described by using a SPICE equivalent circuit model which is based on the three-level rate equations. Effects of some laser diode parameters and dc and rf drive conditions on the full-width half maximum (FWHM) of gain switched pulses are investigated. It is shown that FWHM of pulses decrease as the rf current increased whereas these pulses increase as the dc bias is increased. FWHM decreases also for small value of gain compression parameter and spontaneous coupling factor. However, the variation in carrier lifetime in the well does not significantly affect the FWHM of generated pulses

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm for Intracavity Bimorph Mirror Control
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: We implement a new technique of intracavity bimorph flexible mirror control that allows to manipulate laser beam parameters (increase power, decrease divergence) and to form a given intensity profile at any distance including far-field. Intracavity mirror surface profile is controlled by number of voltages calculated by means of genetic algorithm combined with hill-climbing one. Then the traditional Fox-Li approach is applied. It is numerically shown the possibility of successful formation of Bessel Gauss beam shape in near field and experimental extracavity M2-factor reduction almost in 4 times.

articleTitle: Continuously Tunable Dye Laser for Red and Near IR Regions of Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Absorption, fluorescence, and lasing characteristics of some dyes for laser that continuously tuned in the 650-800 nm region have been studied. Tuning ranges for each of them in a selective cavity with diffraction grating under pumping near the main peaks of their absorption band by booster flashlamp-pumped dye laser are defined

articleTitle: On Possibility of using of Nd: Glass Laser Materials for Pumping on BSF SPA "Physics-Sun"
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The possibility of application of Nd:glass active elements with large sizes for pumping by the concentrated solar flux on the Big Solar Furnace SPA "Physics-Sun" (Tashkent) is considered. For solution of the problem the numerical experiments were carried out and the various variants of laser design had been considered

articleTitle: Remarks on the Slits Experiments
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The fundamental problem of wave-particle duality is analysed. Many physicists' debates did not answer what are photon, electron and other particles. The two-slit experiment has been interpreted as the simplest way to show the wave-particle duality. Then slits experiments are discussed in detail. We conclude that radiation reacts with electrons as the toroidal-like waves

articleTitle: Calculation of the Injection Coefficients for the Superlattice Quantum Cascade Structures
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Numerical self-consistent calculations of the energy levels and wave functions for superlattice quantum cascade structure are performed. Theoretical model for the calculations of the injection coefficients at optical-phonon scattering are suggested

articleTitle: Self-Formation of Train of Attosecond Pulses Under the Optical Shock Wave Formation at Femtosecond Pulse Nonlinear Propagation in Optical Fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Using computer simulation, we investigate an optical wave formation in optical fiber with cubic nonlinear response under the influence of time dispersion of nonlinear response. We show possibility of attosecond pulses train formation at the shock wave front. This train takes place if time dispersion of nonlinear response influences significantly on laser pulse propagation in optical fiber. The influence of frequency modulation is considered as well. Our analysis is based on original transformation of well-known generalized nonlinear Schrodinger equation with temporal derivation from nonlinear response. For computer simulation we use conservative difference schemes, which allow us to make simulation with big accuracy

articleTitle: Shape Transformation of Wave Beams Falling on Quasiperiodic Media
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Bragg structures with distortion of periodicity is considered. Effects of scattering the wave beams falling at oblique angles are theoretically investigated. Methods of characteristic matrices and plane-wave decomposition are used for obtaining angular and spatial distribution of reflected and transmitted wave beams. Magnitudes and phases of scattered fields are analysed. Phenomena of anomalous behaviour of group shifts (decreasing and negative ones) are observed for Bragg structures with different type of distortions

articleTitle: Simple Laser Microinterferometer for Spaceborne Measurements
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Laser interferometer consists of laser, point-like mirror, forming aberration-free beam of light (reference beam), and analyzer beam reflecting by a mirror system to be tested. The analyzer beam is directed to viewing screen or CCD, and it is recombined with the reference beam to produce a system of Twyman-Green fringes. Microinterferometer is very small, simple and lightweight, that is why it is especially recommended for testing optics of the space telescopes in the space, and extreme UV lithography

articleTitle: Synchronization of Multi-Frequency and Chaotic Lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Coherent regime of operation of two optically coupled multi-frequency CO lasers is received for the first time. Generation spectrum of lasers is measured and frequencies locking band is determined. Results of the investigation of radiation synchronization in a system of two chaotic unidirectional ring CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> lasers with optical coupling and periodic pump modulation is presented

articleTitle: Generation of Spatial Gap Solitons within One-Dimensional Photonic Lattices in Lithium Niobate by Mutually Incoherent Light Beams
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The effect of formation of spatial gap solitons by mutually incoherent laser beams within one-dimensional photorefractive photonic lattices in iron-doped lithium niobate is experimentally investigated and discussed

articleTitle: Automatic Measurement System using a Laser Scan Instrument for Ceramic Bearings
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: Ceramic bearings are rolling elements used in many mechanical applications (e.g., fans, motors, etc.). For the purpose of mass production and quality control of ceramic bearings, we have developed an automatic measurement system using a laser scan instrument. The system includes a laser scan instrument, a conveyer platform, automatic feeders, and a personal computer. To provide precise measurement, the laser scan instrument LSM6100 was chosen because our ceramic bearings are relatively small in size. In addition, the conveyer platform is a sloped platform that conveys ceramic bearing and the automatic feeders are used to control the flow of each ceramic bearing. The experimental design includes automatic measurement software on the computer that controls all the mechanisms and records all the laser-scan readings (i.e., diameters of ceramic bearings) for data analysis. In this study, our preliminary results demonstrate that our system offers an effective solution for fully automatic and precise measurement of ceramic bearings that could be potentially used in industry

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of the Different Ways of Cells Illumination and Computer Processing of the Obtained Information
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The possibilities of interference laser microscopy and image computer processing application to investigations of cell reactions external factors are studied. The studies were realized in human buccal epithelium cells. Te illustrations demonstrating the effectiveness of proposed approaches are presented

articleTitle: Polarization-Independent Microcavity with Two Phase Layers
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: In this work microcavity model of tunable VCSEL is produced. The microcavity structure with active region limited by liquid crystal phase layers. Polarization independence is achieved by setting different preorientation of liquid crystal molecules in two layers. The resonance wavelength tuning possibility of such microcavity is investigated. Estimation of the tuning on the modal threshold gain is performed.

articleTitle: Dynamics of Crater Growth During Laser Action on Transparent Dielectric with Plasma Formation on Both Sides of a Target
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: A study was made of the dynamics of craters growth when a millisecond light pulse with a complex temporal profile interacted with the surfaces of transparent insulator when plasma formed on the both sides of the irradiated sample. The effective growth of craters was found to last no more than 100 mus and it consisted of two stages. In the first stage the area of the damage region increased while its depth remained practically constant, whereas in the second stage the crater growth was three-dimensional

articleTitle: Influence of Low Intencity Laser Radiation on Functions of Mitochondria in Rats' Liver
publicationTitle: 2006 International Workshop on Laser and Fiber-Optical Networks Modeling
abstract: The work deals with the investigation of interaction of the low intensity laser radiation and a mitochondria in rats' liver. It is observed that under the action of 1 mW power He-Ne-laser irradiation on the suspension of mitochondria breathing speed increases with succinat of non-phosphorylating and phosphorylating mitochondria. Such effects can be used in biotechnology, particularly, for cultivation of cells and tissues
